div.head: Wi 28
div.ab: Gif feorran cumen man oþþe fræmde buton wege gange ⁊ he þonne nawðer ne hryme ne he horn ne blawe, for ðeof he bið to profianne: oþþe to sleanne oþþe to alysenne.
Gif feorran cumen man oþþe fræmde buton wege gange, ⁊ he þonne nawðer ne hryme ne he horn ne blawe, for ðeof he bið to profianne: oþþe to sleanne oþþe to alysenne.
Gif feorran[-]cumen man oþþe fræmde buton wege gange, ⁊ he þonne nawðer ne hyrme ne he horn ne blawe, for ðeof he bið to profianne, oþþe to sleanne oþþe to alysenne.
Wenn ein fernher gekommener Mann oder ein Fremder ausserhalb der Strasse hingeht und er dennoch weder ruft noch Horn bläst, so ist er als Dieb zu erachten: entweder zu erschlagen oder auszulösen.
If a man who has come from afar or a stranger goes off the road and nevertheless neither shouts nor blows a horn, he is to be considered a thief: either to be slain or to be redeemed.
If a man from afar, or a stranger, quits the road, and neither shouts, nor blows a horn, he shall be assumed to be a thief, [and as such] may be either slain or put to ransom.
If a man from a distance or a foreigner goes off the track, and he neither shouts nor blows a horn, he is to be assumed to be a thief, to be either killed or redeemed.
If a man [who is] come from afar or a stranger should go off the track, and he then neither calls out nor does he blow a horn, he is to be regarded as a thief, either to be killed or to be redeemed.

note.label: echoes
note.quote: at least one of his laws was echoed by Wihtræd ... Wi 28/Ine 20

note.label: practically identical
note.quote: cap. 20 of Ine’s laws is practically identical with cap. 28 of Wihtred’s laws

note.label: repeated nearly verbatim; perhaps common original
note.quote: A clause repeated nearly verbatim in both texts (Ine §20; Wihtred §23 [L28]) … may instead “stem from a common original.” | she affirms (given the assumed dates of the two codes) that Wihtred §23 [L28] is derived from Ine.

note.label: echoes
note.quote: the “echoed” clauses raised by Wormald (Ine §20/Wihtred §23 [L28], …) … with the exception of Ine §20/Wihtred §23 [L28], the echoes seem faint indeed

note.label: contradicts
note.quote: Ine §20/Wihtred §23 [L28] also seems to contradict Ine §28 – as it does Wihtred §21 [L26]

note.label: =; perhaps from a common source
note.quote: After Ine §20 (=Wihtred §23 [L28]) … its derivation from some source common to both … seems more probable than its transmission from Ine to Wihtred.

note.seg: Der Satz lautet grossenteils wie Ine 20, wo Einzelnes erklärt wird; vgl. o. Einl. 7. 11. Zu feorran cumen vgl. Grimm RA S. 5; dieses Wort braucht auch Ine 20 Rb. Ine 21 scheint, weil auch der Nordischen Parallele eigen und sachlich zugehörig, ursprünglich, also Ines Form vollständiger (auch in den Worten geond wudu). Auch scheint der Satz in Wi, als am Schlusse stehend, ein blosses Anhängsel. Gegen die Annahme, die bei einem Paragraphen über Fremde nahe läge, daß die Kirche, etwa eine Synode, die Vermittlerin sowohl für Wi wie für Ine gewesen sei, spricht die vulgarsprachliche Form wie der fremdenfeindliche Sinn, während die Kirche vielmehr den Verkehr zwischen den Kleinstaaten förderte

The clause reads largely like Ine 20, where individual points are explained; cf. above Introduction 7. 11. On feorran cumen cf. Grimm RA p. 5; Ine 20 Rb. also uses this word. Ine 21 seems original, since it is also found in the Norse parallel and belongs to the subject matter, and Ine’s form therefore more complete (also in the words geond wudu). Moreover the clause in Wi, standing as it does at the end, seems a mere appendage. The supposition — which would suggest itself for a section on strangers — that the Church, say a synod, was the intermediary for both Wi and Ine is contradicted both by the vernacular form and by the hostility to strangers in its sense, whereas the Church, rather, promoted intercourse between the small kingdoms
